purpose: Upgraded illustrated 2D pizzeria gameplay screen references. Art-direction proposals, not approved production assets or an implemented UI.
reference_review: Papa's Pizzeria recording and frame sheets supplied in pizza.zip
Individual topping frame pizza_0240.jpg, baking frame pizza_0330.jpg, cutting frame pizza_0400.jpg, order frame pizza_0160.jpg
User's rejected Roblox prototype bake and order screenshots
direction: Large directly interactive food/work surface; compact persistent ticket rail, oven status, and station navigation; original illustrated mint/coral/ivory art, appealing ingredient detail and controlled highlights.
production_rules: All visible artwork must be generated through ChatGPT image generation or Higgsfield. Claude codes integration, game logic and animation, not replacement art.
If art is missing, create an asset request; do not synthesize shapes, SVG, CSS, procedural meshes or code-drawn stand-ins as visible game art.
Code may position, crop, mask and animate approved art and supply live text and invisible input regions.
Text is baked into these reference images only for reviewing the mockups. Production labels, numbers, timers and localized text must remain live.
These references do not prove animation feel, mobile touch usability or runtime performance. Those require implementation and playtesting.
Concepts are unapproved until Lawson selects the direction. They do not reinstate the rejected v1 style guide.

screens.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create ONE polished, full-screen LANDSCAPE 16:9 gameplay UI reference for a modern 2D pizza-making game, showing the TOPPING STATION. This must read instantly as a playable illustrated cooking-game screen, NOT a photograph or interior concept painting.

Input image 1 is a Papa's Pizzeria gameplay frame: use its functional composition only — big overhead pizza to manipulate, individual ingredient containers within reach, narrow order ticket rail. Do not copy its graphics, logo, or old muted brown styling. Input image 2 is the user's REJECTED current prototype: use it only to understand persistent four station tabs and two oven indicators. REPLACE its oversized brown rectangles, primitive circles, and empty space with finished game art.

STYLE: crisp original flat 2D cartoon game sprites, clean organic silhouettes, restrained colored outlines, smooth two-tone shading, selective small glossy highlights. Vibrant appetizing red sauce, golden cheese and crust, fresh green toppings; a light cool mint work surface with rich coral accents, ivory tickets, dark readable ink. Polished tactile surfaces and rounded controls, sleek and playful without generic mobile-game clutter. No realism, no 3D render, no anime, no humans, no portrait, no dramatic depth of field, no cinematic lighting, no black heavy outlines. Food is beautifully illustrated, not a photographic pizza.

LAYOUT: fill the whole image with the game screen, no device frame, no browser, no outer border. A slim top HUD says 'DAY 3' and shows a small coin counter plus two small oven status widgets, one 'READY', one '32s'. The main 72% of the width is an overhead preparation counter. One LARGE pizza occupies its center, about half the screen height, thick hand-illustrated golden crust, visible creamy cheese and sauce, six distinct delicious pepperoni slices distributed by the player. One ingredient piece near the pizza has a subtle placement highlight, suggesting tactile interaction. A tidy row of FIVE illustrated ingredient trays sits under the pizza within the work surface: pepperoni, mushrooms, basil, olives, peppers. Ingredient art must be distinct and appealing. Do not duplicate bowls.
The rightmost 23% is a slim ticket area: selected ivory ticket '#03' with readable simple requirements 'Pepperoni', '6 slices', 'Regular bake', '6 cuts', tiny illustrative requirement icons, and a small happy face patience meter. Two additional tickets are stacked as small numbered tabs '#04', '#05'. The ticket supports the gameplay; it is not a giant dashboard.
Along the bottom, ONE compact navigation bar: 'Order', 'Topping', 'Bake', 'Cut', with small original illustrated icons. 'Topping' is visibly selected. One prominent but compact coral 'Send to oven' button at lower right, above the navigation. Keep touch controls generously spaced and unobstructed.
Make the food and ingredients the strongest focal points. The mockup must have credible, readable UI hierarchy and finished original 2D artwork. Show only this single gameplay screen, no comparison board, no captions outside it.
